correctness.rationale: Weighted Kirchhoff expansion gives the exact unnormalized Walsh coefficient for each sign pattern. The Lucas parity recurrence proves nonvanishing in residue classes 1,2 modulo three. The explicit period-three vector (1,1,2) annihilates a family of \(4^{n/3}\) different signed reduced Laplacians in class zero. For n divisible by three, a double-count of tree/edge incidences and \(N_{\mathrm{spoke}}=F_{2n}\), together with Lucas modulo four, gives fourfold divisibility at every frequency. Exact integer tests enumerate every sign through n=9 and nullvector signings through n=12. These finite tests support but do not substitute for the complete proof.

originality.rationale: The substantive statement is the complete all-character zero-free classification of the wheel graphic-matroid basis indicator, with period-three signed-Laplacian nullvectors, universal divisibility by four in the singular classes, and at least \(4^{n/3}\) distinct zero frequencies. The general weighted tree determinant and Lucas enumeration are admitted prior, but neither gives this evaluated Fourier support criterion without the new construction and combined parity argument. The complete Benjamin–Yerger manuscript and the directly relevant sections of Constantine–Buliga were compared on their scientific claims, and related published research records were searched for equivalent implications. The comparison is bounded, not a guarantee against unindexed older work.
residual_risks: An older wheel-specific signed Laplacian singularity classification could exist under different terminology.
The general signed-tree determinant is classical, so the research distinction lies in the evaluated all-sign support criterion and modular structure, not the determinant formula.
The colored-forest article was not fully inspected beyond the directly relevant sections; no full-document noncoverage conclusion is made.

value.rationale: The spanning-tree basis set of a wheel is a canonical graphic-matroid object; its full Walsh convolution invertibility is a natural quantitative harmonic-analysis problem not resolved by counting trees. The result gives a complete infinite-family residue classification, an explicit structural cancellation mechanism, a coefficient-wide divisibility law, and exponentially many certified Fourier zeros in each singular dimension. These facts identify a genuine boundary for a natural all-frequency invariant, not a narrow computed numerical curiosity.
